title: Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
authors: Miao D, Hou Z, Ge Y, Qi H
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although many predictive models have been developed or validated for delayed bleeding after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), their methodological quality and clinical utility remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed and critically appraised all available predictive models for this outcome. METHODS: We searched five databases through March 2026 for observational studies that developed or validated prediction models or scoring systems for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD in adults (≥18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST. RESULTS: Of 25,177 records screened, five studies reporting five predictive models were included. The incidence of delayed bleeding ranged from 2.9% to 9.9%. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation areas under the curve [AUCs] ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. All studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, mainly because of inadequate reporting in the predictor, outcome, and analysis domains, although most had low concerns regarding applicability. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review identified five predictive models for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD. Lesion location and size were the most frequently reported predictors. Discriminative performance varied across derivation and validation cohorts, with suboptimal external-validation results. All models had a high risk of bias per PROBAST (low concerns regarding applicability); therefore, their findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Efficacy and safety of single-fraction stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) for the curative treatment of extracranial primary Tumors: A collaborative systematic review on behalf of the SBRT Focus Group of the European Society for Radiotherapy & Oncology (ESTRO).
authors: Cuccia F, Franzese C, Dubash S, Dionisi V, Brunner T, Cellini F, Hörner-Rieber J, Zilli T
abstract: Single-fraction stereotactic body radiotherapy (SF-SBRT) represents one of the most advanced frontiers in modern radiation oncology. While ultra-hypofractionation has entered everyday clinical practice in different fields of the oncological care, curative treatments in one session are increasingly attractive for the potential favorable combination of logistic advantages with safety and clinical outcomes. This collaborative systematic review promoted by the ESTRO SBRT Focus Group in participation with members of different disease-site Focus Groups collects the available data in support of SF-SBRT for the curative treatment of the main extracranial primary tumors. The findings highlight that, for specific anatomical sites, SF-SBRT is both safe and effective though the results emphasize the critical importance of careful patient selection and mandatory technological requirements for treatment planning and delivery. This collaborative work provides a comprehensive overview of current evidence and identifies key knowledge gaps for future investigation and upcoming clinical trials.

title: Outcomes of Tendon Graft Versus Dorsal Capsulodesis Techniques for Chronic Scapholunate Ligament Injury in Adults: A Systematic Review.
authors: Alsanawi HAS, Elansary EAN, Asiri AAS, AlEtebi RAA, Mufti TMA, AlEtebi HAA, Alenazi NMM, Alnazhan ASA
journal: Journal of hand surgery global online
abstract: PURPOSE: Chronic scapholunate interosseous ligament injuries contribute significantly to wrist instability. Surgical management remains challenging, with tendon graft-based reconstruction and dorsal capsulodesis being the most common techniques. This systematic review aimed to compare the clinical and radiographic outcomes of capsulodesis-based versus tendon graft techniques for chronic scapholunate ligament injuries. METHODS: This systematic review was conducted per Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane Library identified eligible comparative studies. Studies comparing tendon graft techniques and dorsal capsulodesis for chronic scapholunate interosseous ligament injuries in adults were included. The Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) tool was used for quality assessment. Because of data heterogeneity and lack of consistent quantitative metrics (eg, means and standard deviations), a narrative synthesis of results was performed. RESULTS: Across six included studies encompassing 298 patients, tendon graft and tenodesis techniques demonstrated variable postoperative outcomes. Notable heterogeneity existed within the tendon graft/tenodesis category itself: modified Brunelli tenodesis outperformed the four-bone weave in pain relief (visual analog scale reduction 4.8 cm vs 3.2 cm), grip strength, range of motion (ROM) preservation (86% vs 60%), and Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder, and Hand (DASH) score improvement (31.5 vs 14.2 points). Scapholunate intercarpal ligament similarly outperformed three-ligament tenodesis across grip strength, ROM (113° vs 82°), and patient-reported outcomes. Dorsal capsulodesis provided consistent pain relief, adequate ROM preservation, and lower surgical failure rates in most series, with no statistically significant differences in patient-reported outcome measures compared to tenodesis groups. Radiographic deterioration was observed across all surgical techniques over long-term follow-up without consistent correlation with clinical symptoms. Overall certainty of evidence was very low per Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) assessment. CONCLUSIONS: Neither tendon graft nor capsulodesis techniques demonstrated consistent superiority; outcome differences were more pronounced within technique subcategories than between groups, highlighting the need for standardized, high-quality prospective trials. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Tendon graft reconstruction and dorsal capsulodesis show comparable outcomes for chronic scapholunate ligament injury. Surgical choice should be individualized based on patient factors, injury characteristics, and surgeon expertise. Given the very low certainty of current evidence, standardized outcome reporting and further high-quality prospective studies are needed.

title: Cannabis use and subsequent onset of manic symptoms and bipolar disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Sanjuan-Ortiz C, Querol P, Aymerich C, Laherran N, Ditlevsen F, Navalón P, Rojo-Bofill LM, Young AH
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bipolar disorder is a disabling psychiatric condition affecting approximately 2% of the population, for which identifying modifiable risk factors prior to illness onset is a research priority. Cannabis use is highly prevalent, yet its role in the development of bipolar-spectrum outcomes remains unclear. Previous reviews have included few studies or combined distinct bipolar-spectrum outcomes, limiting outcome-specific inference. AIMS: To evaluate the association between cannabis exposure and subsequent incident BD and manic/hypomanic symptoms separately and examine potential moderating factors. METHODS: Registered (https://osf.io/s38x4/), PRISMA/MOOSE-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of PubMed and Web of Science from inception to October 2025. We included longitudinal observational studies comparing cannabis-exposed and unexposed individuals without prior BD and assessing subsequent bipolar-spectrum outcomes. We meta-analysed studies with extractable data, calculating the unadjusted risk ratios (RRs) for incident BD and manic/hypomanic symptoms. Random-effects meta-analyses, heterogeneity analyses, subgroup analyses and meta-regressions were performed. Study quality was appraised using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS). RESULTS: Nineteen studies were included (total N = 6,960,517; mean age 23.8 ± 11.8 years; 49% female). Cannabis use was associated with increased risk of BD (RR = 2.46, 95% CI = 1.57-3.84; k = 8; N = 206.572) and manic/hypomanic symptoms (RR = 2.11, 95% CI = 1.07-4.18; k = 6; N = 57,243). Moderator analyses identified significant clinical and methodological sources of heterogeneity. NOS scores ranged from 6 to 9, indicating good to high methodological quality. CONCLUSION: Cannabis use was associated with an increased risk of subsequent bipolar-spectrum outcomes. Routine evaluation of cannabis use alongside prevention strategies, to delay initiation and reduce use, may warranted.

title: Brief social contact videos to promote treatment seeking among young adults with depressive symptoms: Intention change, suicidal ideation, and treatment use in a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Levy T, Kuperberg M, Avrahami M, Wainberg ML, Amsalem D
abstract: BACKGROUND: Young adults with depression often avoid mental health care. Social contact videos may increase help-seeking intentions, but whether intention change leads to treatment use remains unclear, especially among those with suicidal ideation. We examined whether change in help-seeking intentions accounted for treatment use after social contact videos versus a written vignette, and whether this pathway differed by suicidal ideation. METHODS: In this randomized controlled trial, 1545 young adults (aged 18-25 years) with depressive symptoms were recruited via Prolific and randomized to one of three brief videos featuring personal recovery stories or a written vignette with identical content, yielding a 3:1 video-to-written comparison. Help-seeking intentions were measured before, after, and at 30-day follow-up. Treatment use at 30-day follow-up was modeled using structural equation modeling. Suicidal ideation was tested as a moderator of the association between intention change and treatment use. RESULTS: Participants assigned to video showed greater change in help-seeking intentions, and intention change was associated with treatment use. The indirect association through intention change and the total effect were significant. Treatment use was greater with video than with vignette. Conditional indirect effects did not differ by suicidal ideation. However, the association between intention change and treatment use was stronger among participants with suicidal ideation than those without. CONCLUSIONS: Change in help-seeking intentions partially accounted for the association between intervention assignment and treatment use. Brief social contact videos may represent a scalable approach to treatment seeking among young adults with depressive symptoms, including those with suicidal ideation. title: Advanced cell-instructive bio-inks: Engineering multiscale niches for functional tissue formation.
authors: Ng WL, Xu Y, Liu F, Bartolo P
abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has transformed tissue fabrication by enabling the precise spatial organization of living cells and biomaterials into biomimetic tissue constructs. However, advances in manufacturing have outpaced the development of bio-inks capable of actively directing tissue formation. Most existing bio-inks remain optimized for printability, rheological behaviour, and structural fidelity, while providing limited control over the biological processes that govern tissue morphogenesis, functional maturation, and regeneration. This review examines the emerging paradigm of cell-instructive bio-inks, which integrate biological regulation directly into material design to recreate the cellular microenvironments that guide tissue development. We present a unifying framework that classifies these bio-inks according to three complementary regulatory dimensions: biochemical niches that regulate cell fate through molecular signalling and regenerative matrices; architectural niches that direct tissue organization through spatial and structural cues; and metabolic niches that modulate oxygen availability, redox homeostasis, and cellular metabolism. We further discuss strategies for integrating these instructive functions within multifunctional bio-inks, together with scalable manufacturing, and artificial intelligence-assisted bio-ink design. By redefining bio-inks as active regulators of cellular behaviour, this review establishes a conceptual framework for engineering next-generation bio-inks capable of orchestrating tissue development, functional maturation, and regenerative outcomes.

title: Machine learning algorithms empower traditional Chinese medicine: Breakthrough approaches from chemical component analysis to pharmacological mechanism research.
authors: Han Z, Zhao F, Xu H, Zhang Z, Wu J, Zhang Y, Pan J, Li M
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine studies are constrained by complex chemical components and multi-target biological interactions, making conventional analytical methods inefficient for mechanism exploration. As a data-driven technique, machine learning has been widely adopted to tackle diverse complex challenges in TCM research. Nevertheless, most existing reviews merely summarize individual algorithms or scattered application cases, lacking systematic task-based classification and unified operational standards. Based on literature published from 2022 to 2026, this review systematically classifies machine learning applications in TCM into four core research tasks. A task-oriented framework is constructed to match different algorithms with appropriate TCM research scenarios. This paper further establishes a complete standardized workflow covering algorithm selection, model construction and model evaluation to standardize ML applications in TCM research. This review also summarizes the applications of machine learning in TCM quality control, bioactive compound identification, processing analysis, and mechanism elucidation. Furthermore, major bottlenecks in current ML-based TCM studies are analyzed, and feasible optimization strategies are proposed. This review aims to provide clear and practical guidelines for the standardized application of machine learning in future TCM research.

title: Artificial Intelligence in suicide prevention: promise, peril, and clinical implications for clinical practice.
authors: Nobile B, Courtet P
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry is progressing rapidly, with promising yet underexplored applications in suicide prevention. While most existing studies have focused on suicide risk prediction, AI could be applied more broadly across the suicide prevention continuum. This review explores AI's potential in improving the detection of suicidal ideation (SI), enhancing clinician training, and expanding patient access to psychotherapeutic support. Studies suggest that AI models may identify SI more sensitively than clinicians by detecting subtle linguistic or semantic cues. Furthermore, AI-based virtual patients have been shown to improve clinicians' confidence and accuracy in suicide risk assessments, particularly when used alongside traditional training methods. On the patient side, CBT-inspired AI tools offer scalable, on-demand support, but most remain unregulated and clinically unvalidated. Despite their perceived empathy and availability, such tools pose ethical and clinical risks. Many patients use AI tools without professional guidance, a trend clinicians often underestimate. This disconnect calls for urgent regulatory oversight and professional engagement. Without clear clinical validation, AI-based tools may evolve outside medical frameworks, exposing vulnerable individuals to preventable harm. Psychiatry must not only adapt but also lead, ensuring that innovation is harnessed responsibly to serve patients with empathy, safety, and scientific rigor.

title: Localized nanomedicine for urologic cancers: anatomy-guided design and clinical translation.
authors: Zheng H, Yuan Y, Zhang X, Li H, Wang W, Chen Y, Nie S, Bi J
abstract: Bladder, prostate, and renal cancers differ in their anatomical locations, tissue structures, and routes of clinical intervention. Conventional systemic treatments are often limited by nonspecific biodistribution, insufficient tumor accumulation, and toxicity. Localized nanomedicine delivery offers an alternative strategy by using organ-specific anatomical access to increase exposure at the tumor site and reduce systemic distribution. Its success depends on the compatibility of nanomedicine delivery systems with the physiological environment, anatomical characteristics, and procedural requirements of the organ. Here, we compare local nanomedicine strategies for these three cancers and discuss how anatomy can guide their design. We therefore define five design criteria for localized nanomedicines: retention, penetration, responsiveness, targeting, and synergy. For each criterion, describe relevant engineering approaches and applications in individual cancers. We also consider barriers to clinical use, including formulation reproducibility and compatibility with clinical workflows. An approach that combines anatomy, nanomedicine design, and delivery procedures may support their clinical translation for more precise diagnosis and treatment.

title: BCL10 deficiency: Long-term immune reconstitution following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
authors: Ali M, Alazami AM, Al-Mousa H
abstract: BCL10 deficiency is a rare combined immunodeficiency characterized by severe infections, chronic diarrhea, hypogammaglobulinemia, and impaired lymphocyte activation despite preserved lymphocyte counts. We report a novel homozygous BCL10 variant with durable cure and immune reconstitution following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

title: Neuroimaging Biomarkers for Brain Disorder Diagnosis Using Advanced Learning Techniques.
authors: Ion IA, Chira C
abstract: Mental illness is becoming increasingly common in everyday life, affecting a growing number of people. Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) is an effective technique for detecting mental disorders. Resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) analyses spontaneous low-frequency oscillations in the Blood Oxygen Level Dependent signal to examine the functional architecture of the brain. fMRI and rs-fMRI data processing contribute to mapping neural activity in specific brain regions, enabling accurate localization of cognitive functions and improving our understanding of Functional Connectivity and interactions among brain regions. This paper focuses on the use of Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques for fMRI analysis to identify brain features that may be associated with Bipolar Disorder (BD) and Alzheimer's Disease (AD). The first step in the proposed approach is the preprocessing of fMRI and rs-fMRI data using two distinct methods: the first combines Statistical Parametric Mapping and the CONN toolbox for improved results, and the second focuses on the MELODIC software. The proposed approach begins with fMRI and rs-fMRI preprocessing using two pipelines: one integrating Statistical Parametric Mapping (SPM) with the CONN toolbox and another based on the MELODIC framework. The aim is to evaluate how preprocessing choices affect functional connectivity representations and classification performance when combined with classical Machine Learning (ML) methods, namely Support Vector Machines and Random Forests, and the Deep Learning (DL) model AlexNet. Given the altered brain connectivity patterns observed in Bipolar Disorder and Alzheimer's Disease, these methods are employed to assess preprocessing-learning interactions across both disorders. Experimental results emphasize that Connbox-SPM preprocessing combined with AlexNet yields the best results for both mental disorders, with Bipolar Disorder reporting 78.2% accuracy and AD achieving 82.4% accuracy.

title: Error-diagnosis-guided cross-indicator adaptive calibration for near-infrared spectroscopic multi-property prediction of coal quality.
authors: Weng Z, Li J, Yuan L
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) coal-quality datasets often contain many repeated spectra acquired from the same coal samples. Ignoring the coal-sample group structure and indicator-dependent error patterns may compromise the reliability of generalization assessment and calibration stability. To address this issue, this study proposes an error-diagnosis-guided cross-indicator adaptive calibration (ED-CIAC) method for NIRS-based multi-property prediction of coal quality. ED-CIAC performs coal-sample-group-level modeling by robustly aggregating repeated spectra and integrating complementary spectral representations to obtain property-specific base predictions. The remaining prediction errors are characterized across properties and value ranges to identify systematic residual structures. Cross-indicator features constructed from the multi-property base predictions are subsequently introduced as complementary calibration information. Candidate calibrators with direct and residual learning modes are evaluated within each training fold, and the calibrator, learning mode, and correction strength are jointly selected for each property according to internal validation performance. Experiments were conducted on 26 batches of NIRS coal-quality data, including 122,983 repeated spectra from 538 independent coal-sample groups, using coal-sample-group-level fivefold cross-validation. The proposed method achieved R2 values of 0.8717 ± 0.0227, 0.9077 ± 0.0120, 0.8112 ± 0.0460, and 0.9000 ± 0.0157 for total moisture (Mt), dry-basis ash (Ad), dry-basis volatile matter (Vd), and net calorific value as received (Qnet,ar), respectively, outperforming conventional chemometric, machine learning, and literature-based comparison methods. These results demonstrate that group-level multi-view base prediction, residual-guided property-specific calibration, and cross-indicator information utilization can improve the reliability of NIRS-based multi-property coal-quality prediction.

title: Kubelka-Munk theory enhances hyperspectral mineral identification for rock heritage.
authors: Peng L, Yang H, Zhou X, Li X, Ju A, Jiang Z, Yang Y
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Accurate identification of minerals is the fundamental task in the protection of rock cultural relics, directly determining the scientific validity and effectiveness of research on weathering mechanisms, disease prediction, and the development of protective materials. However, remote sensing technology is constrained by spatial and observational conditions, making fine in‑situ surveys difficult to achieve. In contrast, proximal hyperspectral imaging overcomes these limitations, providing a reliable technical foundation and data source for in‑situ mineral detection. In this study, a hyperspectral database of common minerals spanning the 900-1700 nm band was established. The diagnostic spectral features of minerals were enhanced through the integration of Kubelka-Munk theory, while efficient mineral identification was achieved by applying machine learning models. Experimental results indicate that diagnostic spectral characteristics are most pronounced within the 1360-1490 nm band. Performance evaluation shows that average efficiency increased by 12.55% and 28.08%, mean F1 scores improved by 12% and 6.14%, mean Kappa values increased by 10.86% and 4.43%, and the F1score of SVM improved by 30%. In addition, spectral detection was conducted on sandstone samples from the Dazu stone carvings, and the experimental results confirmed the accuracy and reliability of the proposed method.

title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis.
authors: Yu H, Hu Z, Tan Q, Wang C, Wang B, Yan Y, Yu Y, Zhang F
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.

title: From passive fillers to active implants: A 3D-printed trilayer piezoelectric scaffold recapitulating native bone hierarchy.
authors: Shan Y, Li S, Wang Y, Lei Y, Wang G, Zhou Q, Lu Y, Wu Y
abstract: Critical-sized alveolar bone defects affect over 10 million patients annually, yet current synthetic bone substitutes act as passive osteoconductive fillers with unpredictable outcomes. Native bone, by contrast, achieves robust regeneration through a trilayered hierarchy of cancellous, cortical, and metabolically active periosteal tissues, with intrinsic piezoelectricity converting mechanical loading into endogenous electrical cues. While piezoelectric biomaterials have emerged as promising active implants, existing homogeneous scaffolds fail to recapitulate native bone's structural complexity and electromechanical coupling; to date, no work has combined this trilayer architecture with piezoelectric functionality in a single construct. Here we report a trilayer bioinspired piezoelectric scaffold fabricated via a two-step conformal 3D printing strategy, composed of a strontium-doped β-tricalcium phosphate (Sr-β-TCP) triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) cancellous layer, a dense cortical layer, and a barium titanate/silk fibroin (BTO/SF) piezoelectric periosteal layer. Under non-invasive low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) stimulation, the scaffold generates bioelectrical signals that support robust osteogenic activity and pro-angiogenic potential in vitro. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that these electrical cues are associated with intracellular calcium influx and upregulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) and Wnt/β-catenin pathways, consistent with enhanced osteogenic differentiation. In a critical-sized bone defect model, the trilayer scaffold with LIPUS achieves substantially superior bone regeneration relative to controls. This work pioneers the integration of native bone hierarchy with piezoelectric functionality into a single active construct, shifting bone tissue engineering from passive filling to bioelectric-guided repair. Coupling structural biomimicry with electroactive stimulation, this strategy holds potential for future bone regenerative applications, including alveolar bone reconstruction.

title: Micellar LYTAC-engineered bionic coatings abrogate RANK-dependent osteocatabolism and boost fibrillogenesis-mimetic mineral accretion for empowering osteoporotic osseointegration.
authors: Zhao Y, Zhou J, He Y, Ren Y, Zhang J, Chen M, Luo Z, Gong Z
abstract: Patients with osteoporosis are highly susceptible to fractures that often require implant fixation and stabilization. However, excessive osteoclast activity under osteoporotic conditions accelerates bone resorption at the bone-implant interface, severely compromising implant osseointegration. RANKL-RANK axis is a central regulator of osteoclast function and emerges as a promising target for osteoporosis treatment, yet current therapeutic options primarily rely on reversible ligand neutralization and can be followed by rebound bone loss after treatment discontinuation. Here, we developed a biomimetic titanium implant coating incorporating RANK-targeted micellar lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) to enhance osseointegration under osteoporotic conditions. Collagen-like peptides (CLPs) were conjugated to bispecific aptamers targeting RANK and the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor (CI-M6PR) through acid-responsive linkers. The resulting conjugates self-assembled into supramolecular LYTACs (CLP-Apt) and were integrated onto hydroxyapatite-modified titanium surfaces. Hydroxyapatite facilitated mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) recruitment, whereas acidic microenvironmental cues triggered CLP-Apt release. Simultaneous engagement of RANK and CI-M6PR on osteoclasts directed RANK toward lysosomal degradation, thereby suppressing osteoclast-mediated bone resorption while promoting MSC osteogenic differentiation and type H vessel formation. Following lysosomal processing, the released CLPs assembled extracellularly into bone matrix-mimetic fibers that chelated Ca2+ and accelerated new bone formation through a fibrillogenesis-mimetic process. By directly degrading RANK while promoting vascularized bone regeneration, this coating provides a localized strategy to overcome osteoclast-driven implant failure and achieve rapid, robust osseointegration under osteoporotic conditions.

title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
authors: Liu Z, Li R, Huang W, Zhang J, Qu Y, Dong W, Liu Y, Li Q
abstract: PURPOSE: Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair. METHODS: Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA. RESULTS: We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+). CONCLUSIONS: Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

title: Reproductive biology and conservation breeding of viverrids in Thailand.
authors: Thongphakdee A, Sangsuri R, Punyatong R, Nakas T, Vechmanus T, Siriaroonrat B, Kamolnorranath S, Susereedumrong J
abstract: In Thailand, nine viverrid species, including the small Indian civet (Viverricula indica), have traditionally been valued for musk used in traditional medicine. Despite their cultural and economic importance, information on their reproductive biology and captive breeding has remained limited. In 2008, Her Majesty Queen Sirikit the Queen Mother initiated a royal conservation project focused on viverrid research and propagation. The program aimed to: (1) establish conservation breeding protocols for small Indian civets, (2) characterize estrous cycles and reproductive hormone profiles, and (3) evaluate male reproductive anatomy and semen characteristics in five viverrid species: small Indian civets, large Indian civets (Viverra zibetha), large-spotted civets (Viverra megaspila), common palm civets (Paradoxurus hermaphroditus), and masked palm civet (Paguma larvata). Results demonstrated that small Indian civets breed throughout the year, with a gestation period of 64-69 days. The breeding program successfully produced 59 kittens, with litter sizes ranging from 1 to 4 offspring. Fecal hormone analyses from nine females monitored over 12 months revealed a polyestrous reproductive pattern, with peak reproductive activity occurring from February to July. The mean estrous cycle length was 18.6 ± 4.2 days. Male reproductive morphology and semen characteristics varied among species, and copulatory plugs were identified in both small Indian civets and large Indian civets during semen collection. The project also extended practical husbandry and breeding knowledge to local farmers through community-based knowledge transfer initiatives. Overall, this study provides novel insights into viverrid reproductive biology and conservation breeding, supporting sustainable population management and reducing pressure from wild capture and hunting.

title: Temporal dynamics of systemic immune cell networks in C57BL/6 mice with collagen-induced arthritis.
authors: Liu L, Hu Y, Liu H, Jin P, Yang S, Zhang H, Wan X
abstract: Collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) model in C57BL/6 (H-2b background) mice provides a valuable model for studying the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). However, the immune mechanism underlying this model remains unclear. This study aims to comprehensively understand the dynamic multi-dimensional characteristics of CIA, especially the temporal changes in immune cell subsets, providing a basis for future research on immune-targeted therapy for RA. The CIA course was divided into onset, peak, and chronic stages based on arthritis scores. Joint pathology was assessed by histology; immune cell subsets in the spleen and lymph nodes were profiled by flow cytometry; and serum cytokines were measured by ELISA. The results revealed distinct stage-specific immune alterations during CIA progression. M1 polarization occurred at the onset stage. DCs were markedly activated at the peak stage, accompanied by elevated frequencies of Th1, Th17, and Tfh cells, while the Breg cell proportions declined. Moreover, DC activation and abundant Th1 and Tfh cells persisted into the chronic stage. Neutrophils remained elevated throughout disease progression to sustain inflammatory responses. Furthermore, upregulated TNF-α and decreased TGF-β1 represented the core cytokine alterations driving CIA pathogenesis. Collectively, this study provided in-depth insights into dynamic immune shifts during CIA progression and offered valuable clues for developing novel RA immunotherapies.

title: Description of a novel phyllobothriidean cestode from the bull shark Carcharhinus leucas (Valenciennes) from the Persian Gulf.
authors: Mastoori M, Haseli M
journal: International journal for parasitology. Parasites and wildlife
abstract: Carcharhinus leucas is a shark species with a global distribution mostly in tropical and subtropical waters, including the Persian Gulf. Knowledge of the cestode fauna of this host continues to grow. In the present study, a new species of phyllobothriidean cestode, Scyphophyllidium persicarium n. sp., is described from the spiral intestine of a bull shark collected off Bandar Lengeh in the Persian Gulf, Iran. The new species is assigned to Category 6 of Scyphophyllidium based on the presence of apical suckers on broad bothridia lacking facial and marginal loculi, the absence of bothridial pores, the presence of gongylate columnar spinitriches on the distal bothridial surface and serrate gladiate spinitriches on the proximal bothridial surface, and the presence of scutes on the strobila. Scyphophyllidium persicarium n. sp. can be distinguished from its congeners by a combination of characters, including total length (11.6-22.9 mm), number of proglottids (30-50), number of testes (80-111), and vitelline follicle distribution (mostly 1 column, rarely 2 columns dorsally and ventrally) in two lateral bands. The new species is further characterized by a euapolytic strobila and the absence of a cephalic peduncle. This discovery brings the total number of Scyphophyllidium species known from C. leucas to five and expands the known diversity of the genus in the Persian Gulf to seven. Globally, infection patterns of Scyphophyllidium species in their shark definitive hosts reveal that a single shark species can harbor multiple congeners either sympatrically or allopatrically, with combinations of species from the same or different morphological categories. The evolution of different microthrix forms among Scyphophyllidium species, particularly across categories 5 through 7, is discussed in light of these infection patterns, with host switching, coupled with adaptation to host intestinal anatomy, proposed as a plausible mechanism explaining microthrix diversity within congeners in a single shark host.

title: Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
authors: Kamada H, Kobayashi K, Yamana H, Fujita N, Namima D, Yamada M, Fujita S, Suto H
abstract: During peroral cholangioscopy-guided electrohydraulic lithotripsy (EHL), stone fragmentation obscures the visual field (the "snowstorm effect"), and visualization quality has been assessed only subjectively. This proof-of-concept study explored the feasibility of a deep-learning method for objectively quantifying visualization quality during EHL and, as an exploratory application, compared viscous gel immersion with saline irrigation. A ResNet-18 model was trained on expert-annotated frames (5-point scale) from three development cases. For independent validation, 120 frames from 12 previously unseen comparison cases were scored by two blinded endoscopists (inter-reader weighted κ = 0.98). The model showed only moderate agreement with their consensus (weighted κ = 0.60; accuracy 70.8%); because the validation sample was enriched for predicted-usable frames, metrics re-weighted to the natural frame distribution gave sensitivity 29.8% and specificity 93.5%, indicating systematic under-detection of usable views. Agreement did not differ systematically between gel and saline frames. The High-Quality View Rate (HQVR) was the proportion of EHL-phase frames scored Good/Excellent. In a patient-level comparison, median HQVR was 22.7% for gel versus 8.4% for saline (exact Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.15, not significant); in post hoc exploratory analyses, a threshold-independent mean predicted score differed (1.65 vs. 1.35, p = 0.005) and the longest continuous usable interval favored gel (median 24.4 vs. 5.2 s). Mild cholangitis occurred in 1/5 gel and 4/7 saline patients. Training such a model is feasible, but it is not yet a validated measurement tool, and the gel-versus-saline signal is hypothesis-generating only. Larger multi-case training and prospective validation are required. Trial Registration: N/A.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Feasibility and potential benefits of daily online adaptive radiotherapy for head and neck cancer without margin reduction using an RTT-only workflow.
authors: Lindegaard AM, Håkansson K, Appelt A, Bernsdorf M, Gothelf AB, Jensen TRB, Mohammad A, Kristensen CA
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Online adaptive radiotherapy (oART) may improve head and neck cancer (HNC) treatment, where anatomical changes during radiotherapy (RT) are common. However, oART is resource-intensive and clinical data are limited. We conducted a prospective feasibility trial implementating an RT technologist (RTT)-led workflow to evaluate dosimetric outcomes, workflow strategies, and intrafractional motion in daily oART. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Ten patients receiving curatively intended oART (33-34 fractions) using standard PTV margins were included (NCT: 07506902). For each fraction, a scheduled plan (original plan recalculated on daily anatomy) and an adapted plan (reoptimized to daily anatomy) were generated, and the preferred plan was delivered. Target coverage (PTV1 V95%), mean dose (Dmean) and maximum dose (Dmax) to selected organs at risk (OAR), treatment time, and baseline target volume were extracted for all fractions. The effect of oART (scheduled- versus delivered plan) was analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Intrafractional motion was assessed weekly. RESULTS: A total of 322 adaptive session were completed. The median treatment time was 29.9 min. The adapted plan was selected in 78% of fractions. oART improved target coverage in 76% of fractions. Dmean decreased for the oral cavity (-2.4 Gy, p < 0.001) but increased for the middle PCM (2.5 Gy, p < 0.001). Dmax increased for the brainstem (2.9 Gy, p < 0.001) and spinal cord (2.2 Gy, p < 0.001). Intrafractional motion was within PTV margins, with few patient-specific exceedances. CONCLUSION: Daily oART for HNC is feasible with improvements in target coverage but modest and inconsistent OAR sparing.

title: Trait-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze-like response resistance.
authors: Kučera J, Makarová M, Vít M, Novák J, Zlámal F, Ráčková L, Fialová Kučerová J, Grulichová M
abstract: The freeze-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals (n = 20) with experienced police rapid response personnel (n = 20). Freeze-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze-like responses. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre- to post-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze-resistance may be associated with stable, trait-like signatures rather than acute stress-responsive processes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze-resistance (r = 0.75, p = 4 × 10-9) and training status (r = 0.71, p = 6 × 10-8), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass (r = 0.57, p = 8 × 10-5). This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms.

title: Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism.
authors: Ahamba IS, Song G, Kinkpe L, Duan Q, Goswami N, Jin Z, Wu J, Dong X
abstract: Intramuscular fat (IMF) significantly influences meat quality, affecting flavor, tenderness, and juiciness. Despite extensive research on livestock such as cattle and pigs, the regulation of IMF in rabbits remains poorly understood. This study establishes a standardized in vitro method for isolating and characterizing intramuscular preadipocytes from the longissimus dorsi muscle of 3-day-old Hycole rabbits using enzymatic digestion and differential centrifugation. Three-day-old neonates were selected for initial protocol development due to their higher progenitor cell abundance and tissue accessibility, which facilitates method optimization and ensures consistent cell yields. Isolated cells displayed typical preadipocyte morphology and expressed key markers, including PREF-1, PPARγ, and Leptin, confirmed by RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence. Upon adipogenic induction, cells exhibited progressive lipid accumulation, as indicated by Oil Red O staining, and showed upregulated expression of PPARG, C/EBPa, and FABP4, confirming their differentiation potential. This study establishes a comprehensive protocol for isolating rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes, providing a foundational tool for investigating the molecular mechanisms of adipogenesis in lagomorphs. The model supports future studies on genetic and nutritional strategies to enhance rabbit meat quality while preserving its lean characteristics.

title: Guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots differentially modulate bacterial respiration and osteoblast mitochondria to resolve infection and foster osteointegration.
authors: Bai X, Qin A, Wang Z, Kong G, Zhang M, Li H, Zhao R, Yu Y
abstract: Implant-associated infections (IAIs) represent one of the most challenging complications following orthopedic implantation. Current antibacterial strategies struggle to achieve complete pathogen eradication while maintaining sustained osteogenic activity at the implant-bone interface. Leveraging the spatial divergence in energy metabolism between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, we designed and synthesized guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots (GQCDs) with confirmed structure. Under non-infected conditions, GQCDs enhance mitochondrial metabolism to promote bone regeneration. In infected microenvironments, GQCDs not only selectively target bacterial membranes and inhibit the respiratory chain to exert potent antibacterial effects, but also downregulate host inflammatory responses and restore mitochondrial function in osteoblasts, thereby creating a favorable microenvironment for bone repair. GQCDs can be stably integrated onto various clinical implant substrates via a coating process. GQCDs-coated implants possessed the dual antibacterial and osteogenic functionalities, which were validated using in vitro co-culture systems and in vivo implant infection models in rats and beagles, offering a promising strategy with encouraging translational prospects to address IAIs.

title: Microbial succession and genome-resolved metabolic functions shape flavor evolution during sauce-flavor Baijiu fermentation.
authors: Niu J, Li W, Chen X, Zhu H, Sun W, Li X, Sun B
abstract: Sauce-flavor Baijiu (SFB) fermentation is characterized by a unique multi-round solid-state process, during which complex microbial succession drives flavor formation. However, the functional differentiation and metabolic mechanisms of microbial communities across successive fermentation rounds remain poorly understood. In this study, the physicochemical properties, microbial assembly, and metabolic profiles of fermented grains (FG) were investigated across seven production rounds (R1-R7). The results revealed that as fermentation rounds progressed, the FG environment evolved toward elevated acidity and reduced pH, driving a directional shift in the microbial community from an initially diverse assemblage to a structure dominated by acid-tolerant Acetilactobacillus, which established pronounced ecological dominance in later rounds. Metabolomic analysis further indicated that this dynamic adjustment of microbial structure drove the evolution of the flavor profile, specifically manifesting as differential accumulation of compounds such as esters, alcohols, and pyrazines across the various rounds. Co-occurrence network analysis demonstrated that positive microbial interactions significantly predominated within the fermentation system, and that community function exhibited a convergent trend as the rounds increased. Furthermore, 158 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were recovered, and metabolic reconstruction elucidated the potential contributions of genera such as Pediococcus, Bacillus, and Oceanobacillus to key metabolic pathways, including glycolysis, phenylalanine metabolism, and pyrazine biosynthesis. This work provides important insights into microbial regulation and quality improvement in SFB fermentation.

title: Tea polyphenols amplify oxidative stress-induced eradication of Staphylococcus aureus by disrupting the hydrogen sulfide (H2S) signaling pathway.
authors: Wang Y, Zhong W, Nie T, Yu B, Ouyang D, Liu Y
abstract: Endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H2S) acts as a pivotal shield for Staphylococcus aureus against oxidative stress. Although tea polyphenols (TPs) are established antibacterial agents, their precise mechanistic impact on H2S-linked redox regulation has yet to be fully elucidated. Here, we test the hypothesis that TPs exert their bactericidal effect on S. aureus by compromising its intrinsic H2S-mediated antioxidant defense system. DL-Propargylglycine (PAG) was used to construct an H2S synthesis-inhibited model (designated WT + inh). The response of this model to TPs was evaluated against that of the wild-type (WT) strain by growth curve analysis, flow cytometry analysis, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). In addition, reactive oxygen species (ROS), antioxidant enzyme activities, including superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT), the oxidative damage marker malondialdehyde (MDA), and the expression of oxidative stress- and sulfur metabolism-related genes were determined. Finally, exogenous H2S supplementation was used to examine whether sulfide could modify the response to TPs. PAG treatment significantly enhanced bacterial susceptibility to TPs, concomitant with increased cell death and exacerbated morphological damage. Intracellular activities of SOD and CAT were reduced, whereas ROS and MDA levels were significantly elevated. Exogenous H2S modulated the growth inhibitory effects of TPs. The TP-associated oxidative damage coincided with changes in H2S-related sulfur metabolism and antioxidant gene expression. These findings support an association between H2S-related antioxidant defense and the susceptibility of S. aureus to TPs, providing a basis for further investigation of H2S metabolism in tea polyphenol-based antibacterial strategies.

title: Salt-dependent osmoadaptation and metabolic responses of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum BS3-1 in fermented bamboo shoots.
authors: Xie L, Zhang X, Shen K, Wang X, Zhou S
abstract: Salt concentration shapes the growth and metabolism of lactic acid bacteria in vegetable fermentations, yet the effects of salt gradients on the fermentation performance of suansun-derived Lactiplantibacillus plantarum BS3-1, together with associated temporal transcriptional changes in BS3-1 and metabolite variation in the fermentation broth, remain insufficiently characterized. Here, BS3-1 was evaluated across a 0-7% (w/w) salt gradient during suansun fermentation. The 0%, 3%, and 5% treatments were selected for time-series transcriptomic analysis of fermentation-derived cell pellets and untargeted metabolomic analysis of fermentation-broth supernatants. The 3% treatment yielded the highest sensory score (79.0/100 versus 72.2/100 in the no-added-salt treatment). On day 7, total acidity was 8.16 g/L at 1% salt and 3.60 g/L at 7%, and viable cells at 7% fell below the detection limit. BS3-1 transcriptional profiles and fermentation-broth metabolite compositions differed among salt treatments. In the 3% versus 0% comparison, 119 differentially expressed genes were shared across four time points, while an average of 598 differential metabolites was identified per time point. WGCNA identified 17 co-expression modules with significant module-trait associations. Association analysis integrating 126 candidate hub genes from four phenotype-associated modules with 30 shared differential metabolites retained 1100 gene-metabolite associations (|r| ≥ 0.65, global BH-FDR < 0.05). Overall, under the tested conditions, 3% salt provided the most favorable balance among viable-cell persistence, acidification, and sensory quality, while multi-omics analysis revealed covariation among BS3-1 transcriptional responses, fermentation traits, and fermentation-broth metabolite variation.
